title: bug: VS Code Release Agent never sends force and never shows its refusal, so releasing a task whose seat is mid-step (a hung or crashed worker) is refused STEP_LEASE_HELD with no message and no override (the VS Code twin task-0f2e958f left to a separate row)
description:
Filed by hunt #14 (task-d5d58972, 2026-11-03, architect-1dd28c7c). IDE follow-through on the release_task force rules (task-0adea941, task-c8d6dbd5) and on the JetBrains fix task-0f2e958f (completion 1cf76839). That row put moe-vscode out of scope ("a VS Code twin can be filed separately"), and its QA review closed with "Follow-up: the VS Code twin (VSC-6) is not filed." This is that row.

PROBLEM (HEAD 942717bc)
- The VS Code side:
  - moe-vscode/src/panels/TaskDetailPanel.ts:495-514 (case 'releaseAgent') shows one modal, then calls `this.client.releaseTask(this.taskId, RELEASED_FROM_BOARD)` (:511).
  - MoeDaemonClient.releaseTask (moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts:1226-1240) has no force parameter. Its doc comment says "`force` is never sent" (:1232).
- The daemon side:
  - /ws RELEASE_TASK forwards force only when it is === true (packages/moe-daemon/src/server/WebSocketServer.ts:738-748).
  - Without force, util/claimGuards.ts:266-280 (assertNoLiveLease) refuses any row whose assignee has an IN_PROGRESS step: NOT_ALLOWED / STEP_LEASE_HELD.
  - Since 0adea941 and c8d6dbd5, force is still honoured for a caller with no workerId, which is the /ws board path (tools/releaseTask.ts:141-152 gates only a PRESENT workerId). So the board override is meant to work, and it does in JetBrains.
- The refusal is only logged. MoeDaemonClient.ts:2131-2150 fires onError, but:
  - TaskDetailPanel.handleClientError (:401-413) returns unless the operation is APPROVE_TASK;
  - BoardViewProvider's subscriber (:48-55) only toasts approvals.
- The JetBrains reference is moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/BoardRelease.kt:
  - stepLease (:47-53);
  - release(...) (:62-84): the first confirmation, then a second force confirmation, then a re-check that the latest cached task still shows the SAME lease (else nothing is sent and the user is told), then send(true).
  - Its texts are MoeBundle.properties:104-106 (moe.message.releaseAgentForce, releaseAgentForceTitle, releaseAgentForceStale).

EVIDENCE
1. Daemon side: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-d5d58972/B/zzHuntB_clientFrames.test.ts (with zzHuntB_harness.ts), from packages/moe-daemon/src/__hunt__/ of a `git archive 942717bc` snapshot. `npx vitest run src/__hunt__/zzHuntB_clientFrames.test.ts` → 3 passed, recording:
   HUNT VS CODE FRAME -> DAEMON REPLY: {"type":"ERROR","message":"[STEP_LEASE_HELD] Task task-leased is leased by worker-hung with step step-1 IN_PROGRESS; only a governor or a human may override that lease (moe.release_task force), and only for a confirmed-dead holder","operation":"RELEASE_TASK","code":-32003,"codeName":"STEP_LEASE_HELD","context":{"taskId":"task-leased"}}
   HUNT JETBRAINS FORCE FRAME -> DAEMON REPLY: {"type":"TASK_UPDATED","status":"WORKING","assignedWorkerId":null}
2. VS Code side: the real TaskDetailPanel and MoeDaemonClient, with the daemon's ERROR frame delivered verbatim. Run from the moe-vscode dir of a whole-tree `git archive 942717bc` snapshot: `NODE_PATH=<checkout>/moe-vscode/node_modules node --test --test-reporter=tap tests/zzHuntB_vscodeRefusals.test.cjs` (repro at /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-d5d58972/B/zzHuntB_vscodeRefusals.test.cjs). Output:
   # FRAME SENT: [{"type":"RELEASE_TASK","payload":{"taskId":"task-leased","reason":"Released from board"}}]
   # onError FIRED: [{"operation":"RELEASE_TASK","message":"[STEP_LEASE_HELD] …","code":-32003,"codeName":"STEP_LEASE_HELD","context":{"taskId":"task-leased"}}]
   # TOASTS/MODALS: {"infos":[],"warnings":[[<the one Release Agent confirm modal>]],"errors":[],…}
   not ok 2 - VS Code Release Agent on a mid-step seat: no force ever sent, and the STEP_LEASE_HELD refusal is never shown
   The architect's re-run is in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-d5d58972/me/vscodeRefusals.rerun.txt.

FIX DIRECTION (moe-vscode only, a port of BoardRelease)
- The first confirmation stays as it is.
- If the task AS RENDERED has a non-blank assignedWorkerId and an IN_PROGRESS step (the first one, as claimGuards.inProgressStep and BoardRelease.stepLease use), ask a second modal with the JetBrains bundle texts (releaseAgentForce / releaseAgentForceTitle).
- Then re-read the latest cached task. If it no longer shows the same holder and step, send nothing and show releaseAgentForceStale. Otherwise send force:true.
- Give MoeDaemonClient.releaseTask an optional `force`, and put `force: true` on the frame only when it is true. A plain release frame stays byte-identical to today, which wire-parity.test.cjs A1 pins.
- Show a RELEASE_TASK refusal whose context.taskId is this panel's task (context.taskId is already on the allowlist, MoeDaemonClient.ts:99-115), instead of only logging it.
- Pin the three new texts to MoeBundle.properties, the way tests/task-release.test.cjs already pins releaseAgent.

FILES (planner to confirm)

- moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts (releaseTask only)
- moe-vscode/tests/task-release.test.cjs (extend), and moe-vscode/tests/wire-parity.test.cjs if its RELEASE_TASK arm needs a force case

implementationPlan.description:
TaskDetailPanel ports JetBrains BoardRelease.release (moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/BoardRelease.kt:47-84; mem:decision-board-force-release-recheck) and shows its own RELEASE_TASK refusals. All edits are in moe-vscode/src/panels/TaskDetailPanel.ts. Add NO import and export nothing new: a new value import breaks every peer test's strict require map (mem:gotcha-vscode-panel-strict-require-map).
(a) In the 'Release Agent' section (:255-274), add RELEASE_AGENT_FORCE, RELEASE_AGENT_FORCE_TITLE ('Force Release Agent') and RELEASE_AGENT_FORCE_STALE, copied byte-exact from moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties:104-106 (moe.message.releaseAgentForce, moe.message.releaseAgentForceTitle, moe.message.releaseAgentForceStale). Name them in the section comment.
(b) Add module-scoped `formatBundleText(template: string, ...values: string[]): string` = `template.replace(/\{(\d)\}/g, (match, index: string) => values[Number(index)] ?? match)`. It is one pass, so a value that looks like a placeholder is never re-scanned, and a repeated {0} (the force text has two) gets the same value. Use it for the existing confirm text too, replacing the inline /\{([01])\}/g replace (same output; the existing one-pass row pins it).
(c) Add module-scoped pure `stepLease(task: Task | undefined): { holder: string; stepId: string } | null`. It mirrors packages/moe-daemon/src/util/claimGuards.ts assertNoLiveLease + inProgressStep for a /ws caller with no workerId, and BoardRelease.stepLease: holder = task.assignedWorkerId when it is a non-empty string; step = the FIRST implementationPlan entry whose status === 'IN_PROGRESS' (guard a missing or non-array plan with Array.isArray); otherwise null.
(d) Rewrite case 'releaseAgent' (:495-515) in this order:
1. Keep the current read and the 'No agent is assigned to this task.' info for a missing task or blank worker id.
2. BEFORE the first await, capture `const lease = stepLease(current)` and `const title = current.title`. The task the user is confirming alone decides force; the cache is re-read only to refuse a stale force.
3. Show the first modal exactly as today (text, { modal: true }, RELEASE_AGENT_LABEL). Any other answer stops.
4. No lease: call `this.client.releaseTask(this.taskId, RELEASED_FROM_BOARD)` with exactly these two arguments (an existing stub row compares the argument list).
5. A lease: show a second modal, `vscode.window.showWarningMessage(formatBundleText(RELEASE_AGENT_FORCE, lease.holder, lease.stepId, title), { modal: true }, RELEASE_AGENT_FORCE_TITLE)`. Any other answer stops with nothing sent.
6. Then compute `stepLease(this.findTask())`. If it is null, or its holder or stepId differs, call `vscode.window.showWarningMessage(formatBundleText(RELEASE_AGENT_FORCE_STALE, lease.holder, lease.stepId))` with that one argument and send nothing. Otherwise call `this.client.releaseTask(this.taskId, RELEASED_FROM_BOARD, true)`.
7. A false return from either send shows the existing 'Not connected to Moe daemon — agent was not released.' warning.
The handler touches no client member except currentState (through findTask) and releaseTask, because the stub client in task-release.test.cjs throws on anything else.
(e) handleClientError (:401-413): FIRST, when event.operation === 'RELEASE_TASK', call `vscode.window.showErrorMessage('Agent was not released: ' + event.message)` only if event.context?.taskId === this.taskId, and return for every RELEASE_TASK event. A context-less RELEASE_TASK event is the client's own send failure (wire-parity A4): releaseTask already returned false and the not-connected warning reported it, so the panel shows nothing more. The APPROVE_TASK branch stays as it is.
Error handling: everything stays inside handleWebviewMessage's try/catch, so an exception still shows 'Task action failed: ...'. Edit with the seat's own editor, never a shell write.

- `RF3 decline: ` On that mid-step task, dismissing the first modal shows one modal and sends nothing. Confirming it and dismissing the force modal shows two modals and sends nothing. No info or error in either case.
- `RF4 plain: ` For steps step-1 COMPLETED + step-2 PENDING, and for an empty plan: one modal only, and sent is exactly ['{"type":"RELEASE_TASK","payload":{"taskId":"task-release","reason":"Released from board"}}'].
- `RF5 stale: ` From onWarning at the force modal, deliver in turn: a TASK_UPDATED with holder 'w-new' on step-2; one with step-2 COMPLETED and step-3 IN_PROGRESS; one with no IN_PROGRESS step; one with assignedWorkerId null; and a TASK_DELETED. Each sends nothing, and the third warning is exactly [expectedText(stale, 'w-mid', 'step-2')]. A TASK_UPDATED that only renames the title still sends the one force frame.
- `RF6 refusal: ` Deliver the daemon's verbatim STEP_LEASE_HELD ERROR frame from the task description, with taskId 'task-release', holder w-mid and step step-2. It gives exactly one showErrorMessage: 'Agent was not released: ' + its message. The same frame for 'task-other', an UPDATE_TASK ERROR for this task and a context-less RELEASE_TASK ERROR show nothing.
Fast loop, outside npm: from the task worktree's moe-vscode, `NODE_PATH=/mnt/d/projexts/moes/moe-vscode/node_modules node --test tests/task-release.test.cjs tests/wire-parity.test.cjs`. Never run npm in the shared checkout. Edit with the seat's own editor, never a shell write.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: 1) Retry with force after a STEP_LEASE_HELD refusal: rejected. VS Code can now match a refusal by context.taskId, but a retry would force a lease the user never saw named, could strip a different live seat, and breaks parity with JetBrains, which decides before sending (mem:decision-board-force-release-recheck). 2) Stub-client panel tests asserting releaseTask arguments: kept for the existing rows, but not used for the new ones. The DoD asks for frames and byte-identity, so RF2-RF6 drive the REAL MoeDaemonClient, as the hunt repro did. 3) A shared util module for stepLease/formatBundleText: rejected. A new value import in TaskDetailPanel.ts breaks every peer harness's strict require map. 4) No wire-parity row: rejected. That file is the RELEASE_TASK wire contract (A1-A4), and RF7 alone pins the `=== true` strictness that panel paths cannot reach. It is the 5th file and stays within the standard band. 5) Epic-final scope: epic-be924fb8 is a rolling bug bucket with 229 rows, and isEpicFinal is the highest-order fallback. Full regression for the only affected package (the whole moe-vscode suite plus tsc) is the gate. The adversarial pass covers this diff, not the epic.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: The daemon's /ws ERROR frame carries context.taskId copied from the request payload (WebSocketServer.ts:1213-1232). The error-context allowlist applies only to MoeError.context keys, so a RELEASE_TASK refusal IS matchable to the panel's task. The VS Code client replaces cached task objects on TASK_UPDATED and filters them on TASK_DELETED, so a click-time `current` is effectively a snapshot. Still, capture holder and stepId as strings before the first await. BoardViewProvider and PlanReviewPanel ignore every non-APPROVE_TASK error, so TaskDetailPanel is the only display. In node --test's spec reporter, top-level rows print at column 0 as '✔ <name> (<ms>)', which the gate counts. Dry run on d5431577: the snapshot gate's mechanics pass (756 tests, 0 fail, about 10 s).
planningNotes.risks:
- vm-realm objects (for example the { modal: true } options) fail deepStrictEqual against test-realm ones: compare field by field or with JSON.stringify.
- The panel's vm context in the existing loadModule has no setTimeout. A TASK_UPDATED in RF5 arms the 200 ms debounce, so the live harness must pass timers in, give the webview postMessage, and dispose the panel and client in finally. Otherwise a ReferenceError is swallowed by the client's handleMessage catch, or the node:test child stays alive.
- The existing stub rows use a strict client and compare the plain call's argument list: the plain path must call releaseTask with exactly two arguments and touch no other client member.
- The force text repeats {0}, so substitution must be one pass, and the test's expectedText must be an independent split/map.
- The gate's count regex needs top-level rows named exactly 'RF<n> <lowercase word>: '. 'A5:' and 'F1:'-'F6:' already exist elsewhere, hence the RF prefix.
- Rails: never run npm in the shared checkout, never pattern-kill, and write tracked files only with the seat's own editor.
